title: Personal OKRs weekly check-in — week of 2026-04-06
content:
Week: 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-10
Context: personal OKR check-in and notes. Mostly a scratchpad for progress on the batching/quantization work and follow-ups for next week.

OKR alignment (Q2):
- Objective: Reduce inference cost for hosted API customers while maintaining p95 latency SLOs and output quality.
  - KR1: 12% unit cost reduction on recurrent text workloads by end of Q2. (baseline = Jan 2026 cost per 1M tokens)
  - KR2: Keep p95 latency regression < 5% across top 5 routes during rollout of batching changes.
  - KR3: Deploy quantization profile recommendations for top 3 model families in catalog and validate with evals.

This week — progress:
- Batching PoC (local): merged stream of small changes that enable grouping by route + model-compatibility. Measured ~9% token/sec throughput improvement on synthetic chat workloads.
  - Notes: gains larger when seq length distribution narrow; tail requests still cause fragmentation.
- KV prefix caching: prototype toggles per-route. Observed 6% request-level latency improvement on routes with high prefix reuse (assistant-chat).
- Quantization experiments: ran post-training 4-bit quant on Llama2-13B variant; quality regression small on summarization eval (ROUGE delta ~ -0.7).
- Cost sim: updated cost model spreadsheet (linked to PROJ-1124) with batching/kv assumptions -> projected 8–10% unit cost improvement if rollout is staged across routes.
- Documented rollout plan for canary: route selection, traffic %s, rollback criteria. Draft in CONFLUENCE-ENG-RUNTIME-78.

Metrics & signals observed (this week):
- Synthetic throughput: +9% tokens/sec after batching PoC (local).
- Summarization eval on 4-bit quant: ROUGE-L -0.7, human spot-checks (5 examples) ok but more edge cases.
- KV cache hit-rate on assistant-chat testbed: 37% -> target 45% after tuning TTLs and prefix matching.
- Local p95 latency: +2% variance in some configs; still < 5% threshold.

Blockers / Risks:
- Model compatibility matrix still incomplete — need to ensure fallback policies when quantized variant not acceptable for a route. (Ticket: PROJ-1124)
- Ops concerns about persistent KV storage for private deployments — need SRE input on memory/cpu tradeoffs.
- Eval coverage limited: need more long-form QA and adversarial prompts to validate quality regression of quantized models.

Next week — plan / TODOs:
- Finish model compatibility matrix (owner: me). Deliverable: spreadsheet mapping model family -> supported quant profiles, expected quality delta. Due: 2026-04-13.
- Add canary automation: traffic shift + automatic rollback when p95 exceeds baseline by >5% or when quality regression detected in eval set. Pair with Hunter (SRE) to get infra hooks.
- Expand evaluation set: add 100 long-form prompts + edge cases for summarization and instruction-following. Recruit 2 folks for human eval (Samira agreed to help).
- Tune KV prefix TTL logic and re-run cache hit experiments. Goal: hit-rate >= 45% for assistant-chat by 2026-04-20.
- Draft email & short runbook for product owners describing what to expect during canary rollout.

Retrospective notes (quick):
- What went well: quick local PoC iteration, decent cross-team feedback from product on route prioritization.
- What didn't: underestimated eval time; human checks are bottleneck. Need to budget more for quality validation.
- Action: build small eval harness to triage obvious regressions automatically (spike to implement next week).

Questions / asks for manager:
- Can we get 1 headcount quarter allocation (0.2 FTE) from infra to help with canary infra automation? This would speed rollout and reduce manual on-call steps.
- Approval to run a small internal customer trial on 2 low-risk routes once canary is stable. Need legal signoff for data handling on private routes — can you connect me to compliance?

Notes to self (scrappy):
- Keep quick notes in this doc; once final, copy key parts to Confluence page and update PROJ-1124.
- Remind Samira to run the human eval batch next Wed.
- Check in with Hunter about memory budgets for persistent KV caches in dedicated clusters.

Relevant links / tickets:
- PROJ-1124 (batching + quantization epic)
- CONFLUENCE-ENG-RUNTIME-78 (rollout plan)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1023

Quick snapshot for manager 1-line email:
- "This week: batching PoC + KV prototype → projected 8–10% unit cost improvement; next week: finish compatibility matrix, canary automation, expand evals. Need 0.2 FTE infra help + compliance intro for small trial."

End of note.
